title: Deploy local agents everywhere with LFM2.5-2.6B
gist: Liquid AI released LFM2.5-2.6B, a 2.6B-parameter on-device agentic model trained on ~34T tokens with a four-stage post-training pipeline culminating in multi-turn RL run inside real agent harnesses. It matches or beats models up to ~4x larger on instruction following and tool use while decoding at 220 tok/s on an M5 Max in under 2.5 GB of memory, explicitly targeting workloads that would otherwise carry a cloud inference bill.

insights.claim: Liquid AI is positioning small on-device models as a way to remove cloud inference cost entirely from agentic workloads, framing privacy and zero marginal inference cost as the two commercial arguments for edge deployment.
insights.speaker: Leonie Monigatti
insights.so_what: If capable agents run free on client hardware, the per-token cloud inference revenue pool for high-volume simple agent tasks shrinks; watch inference-billing exposure at API providers.
insights.quote: This enables developers to deploy agents everywhere, keep data private on the device, and scale usage without a cloud inference bill.
insights.locator: LFM2.5-2.6B is built to power capable agents

insights.claim: The recommended use case for LFM2.5-2.6B is explicitly high-volume on-device agent workloads rather than general chat, implying the edge-model market is being segmented by throughput economics rather than capability ceilings.
insights.speaker: Leonie Monigatti
insights.so_what: Segmenting by volume rather than quality suggests edge models will take the long tail of repetitive agent calls first, not flagship reasoning.
insights.quote: Reach for LFM2.5-2.6B when you need on-device agents for high-volume workloads.

insights.claim: A phone-class decode rate of 30 tokens per second is treated as the practical threshold at which agents become usable on handsets, giving a concrete hardware bar for mobile agent deployment.
insights.speaker: Leonie Monigatti
insights.so_what: A 30 tok/s bar lets you screen which shipping mobile SoCs can host agents today and which need another silicon generation.
insights.quote: At 30 tokens/s, it allows you to run capable agents even on a phone.

insights.claim: LFM2.5-2.6B was pre-trained on roughly 34 trillion tokens with a mid-training phase extending context to 128K, showing that sub-3B models are now being fed data budgets previously reserved for frontier-scale training.
insights.speaker: Leonie Monigatti
insights.so_what: Massive over-training of tiny models converts training compute into permanently cheaper inference — a structural shift in where AI compute demand sits.
insights.quote: LFM2.5-2.6B is pre-trained on ~34T tokens, with a mid-training phase that extends the context window to 128K.
insights.locator: How we built a reliable agentic model for edge devices

insights.claim: Post-training uses a four-stage pipeline — two rounds of agent-weighted supervised fine-tuning, per-domain specialist teachers, multi-domain on-policy distillation into one student, and multi-turn agentic RL — rather than a single instruction-tuning pass.
insights.speaker: Leonie Monigatti
insights.so_what: Multi-teacher distillation plus harness RL is becoming the standard recipe for squeezing frontier behavior into small models; expect competitors to copy it within quarters.
insights.locator: Post-training then turns the base model into an agent

insights.claim: Training was run inside real agent harnesses such as OpenClaw and Hermes Agent so the model learns compatibility with actual tools, system prompts and multi-turn environments — treating harness compatibility as a trainable property rather than an integration detail.
insights.speaker: Leonie Monigatti
insights.so_what: If models are RL-trained against specific harnesses, harness ecosystems gain lock-in power similar to app stores.
insights.quote: Trained inside the most popular agentic harnesses to improve compatibility.

insights.claim: The Harness Proxy component lets Liquid AI run RL against unmodified third-party agent harnesses while still capturing token-level trajectories, removing the need to fork or instrument each harness.
insights.speaker: Leonie Monigatti
insights.so_what: This makes agentic RL scale across the whole harness ecosystem cheaply — a real moat component for whoever builds the tooling.
insights.quote: The Harness Proxy lets us treat agentic harnesses as black boxes with no modification, while transparently capturing the token-level trajectories needed to reconstruct and validate RL training samples.
insights.locator: Actions are executed within a Sandbox Service

insights.claim: At 2.6B parameters LFM2.5-2.6B tops every instruction-following benchmark reported (IFBench 59.17, Multi-IF 80.07, IFStruct 85.49) against Gemma and Qwen models up to 9.7B, indicating instruction adherence scales with training method more than parameter count.
insights.speaker: Leonie Monigatti
insights.so_what: Instruction-following being decoupled from scale undercuts the case for paying frontier prices on structured-output workloads.
insights.quote: LFM2.5-2.6B tops every instruction-following benchmark here, and every tool-use benchmark except BFCLv4, where only the 9.7B Qwen edges ahead.
insights.locator: For your app, the strengths are instruction following

insights.claim: Coding is explicitly conceded as the one domain where larger models keep a clear lead, with LiveCodeBenchv6 at 59.41 versus 69.86 for Qwen3.5-9B — an unusually candid limitation disclosure in a launch post.
insights.speaker: Leonie Monigatti
insights.so_what: Code generation remains a scale-bound workload, protecting large-model demand from edge substitution in the highest-value developer segment.
insights.quote: Coding is the one place the larger models keep a clear lead, so reach for something bigger there.
insights.locator: For your app, the strengths are instruction following

insights.claim: LFM2.5-2.6B scores -29.50 on AA Omniscience versus -74.47 for the 5.1B gemma-4-E2B-it and -50.43 for the 9.7B Qwen3.5-9B, meaning the small model hallucinates materially less than models three to four times its size.
insights.speaker: Leonie Monigatti
insights.so_what: Calibration, not size, drives the knowledge-reliability metric — a signal that small-model deployment risk is lower than commonly assumed.

insights.claim: On the browser-agent benchmark BrowseComp+ run under OpenClaw, LFM2.5-2.6B scores 26.89 against 27.23 for Qwen3.5-9B and just 8.31 for gemma-4-E2B-it, showing real web-agent parity with a model nearly 4x larger.
insights.speaker: Leonie Monigatti
insights.so_what: Browser agents running locally at near-9B quality is the concrete condition for consumer-device agent products shipping without server costs.

insights.claim: Absolute scores on the τ³-Bench Banking task are in the 3–6 range for every model tested including the 9.7B Qwen, indicating that realistic multi-turn domain agents remain broadly unsolved regardless of model size.
insights.speaker: Leonie Monigatti
insights.so_what: Enterprise-grade transactional agents are far from production quality at any size — discount vendor claims of imminent banking automation.

insights.claim: LFM2.5-2.6B decodes at 220 tokens/s on an Apple M5 Max and 113 tokens/s on a Ryzen AI Max+ 395 while fitting in under 2.5 GB of memory, making consumer CPUs a viable agent substrate without a discrete GPU.
insights.speaker: Leonie Monigatti
insights.so_what: Sub-2.5 GB footprints put agents inside the memory budget of shipping laptops and phones, expanding the installed base overnight.
insights.quote: 220 tok/s on an Apple M5 Max and 113 tok/s on an AMD Ryzen CPU, in under 2.5 GB of memory.

insights.claim: On GPU the model reaches nearly 15K output tokens per second at high concurrency, roughly 1.3 billion tokens per day from a single H100, which reframes small models as a server-side throughput play and not only an edge play.
insights.speaker: Leonie Monigatti
insights.so_what: 1.3B tokens/day/H100 sets a hard floor on serving cost that any commercial API pricing for comparable tasks must beat.
insights.quote: reaching almost 15K output tokens per second at high concurrency, roughly 1.3B tokens per day on a single H100

insights.claim: The release shipped with day-one support across llama.cpp, MLX, vLLM, SGLang and ONNX, showing that runtime-ecosystem coverage at launch is now a competitive requirement rather than a follow-on integration.
insights.speaker: Leonie Monigatti
insights.so_what: Day-one runtime coverage compresses adoption timelines; model vendors without it lose the first-mover window on developer mindshare.
insights.quote: LFM2.5-2.6B ships with day-one support across the inference ecosystem, including llama.cpp, MLX, vLLM, SGLang, and ONNX.
insights.locator: Inference speed on CPU and GPU

insights.claim: The model requires transformers>=5.0.0 and both instruct and base checkpoints were published openly on Hugging Face at launch, alongside a WebGPU browser demo running a research agent with no setup.
insights.speaker: Leonie Monigatti
insights.so_what: Open base weights plus in-browser demos lower the trial barrier to near zero, accelerating displacement of paid APIs in prototypes.
